issues.t: Engine stalls without warning while driving
issues.sym: The engine shuts off at speed, while slowing down or when turning. Dash lights may flash first, and you lose power steering and power brake assist. It often restarts after you shift to Park and turn the key again.
issues.why: Owners trace this to several causes on this platform: engine computer software, the front control module, the ignition switch (all covered by separate recalls below) and wiring harness faults. Many cases are never pinned down.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Steer to safety with firm pressure on the wheel and brake. Have a dealer run your VIN for open recalls first, then have stored codes read right after an event.

issues.t: 4.7L V8 can stall from engine computer software (recall)
issues.sym: The engine may stall under certain driving conditions without warning.
issues.why: Software in the engine computer on early 2006 Commanders with the 4.7L V8 could let the engine stall.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Make sure recall H19 was done. The dealer reprograms the engine computer free.

issues.t: Knee can bump the key and shut off the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly shuts off while driving, often after your knee brushes the key or a heavy key ring swings. Airbags, power steering and power brakes may stop working.
issues.why: The ignition switch could be knocked out of the Run position too easily.
issues.next: Take everything but the key off the key ring and have recall P41 done. The dealer replaces the ignition switch free.

issues.t: Ignition key can slip out of Run while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The key sticks between Start and On, or the ignition slips to Accessory or Off while driving and the engine stalls.
issues.why: The ignition switch on some 2008 models built March 2007 to May 2008 could hold the key in the wrong spot.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the dealer replace the ignition switch and key fobs under the recall. It's free.

issues.t: Transfer case can slip into neutral (recall)
issues.sym: A 4x4 Commander parked in Park can roll away because the transfer case has shifted into neutral.
issues.why: An electrical fault could shift the transfer case into neutral on its own.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake. Make sure recall N23 (a free software update) was done. NHTSA recall number: 13V-175.

issues.t: Front control module can stall the engine or kill the wipers (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or won't start, or the windshield wipers stop working.
issues.why: Some front control modules under the hood were built incorrectly.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the dealer inspect and replace the module free if your VIN is included.

issues.t: Sunroof drain tubes leak water inside
issues.sym: Wet headliner, water dripping from the dome light or A-pillar trim, wet carpet, or a musty smell after rain.
issues.why: The sunroof tray drains through tubes in the roof pillars. They clog or come off their fittings, so water overflows into the cabin.
issues.next: Clear the drains with low-pressure air or a trimmer line. If water still gets in, have the drain tubes reattached before mold or wiring damage sets in.

issues.t: Interior door handles crack or snap
issues.sym: An inside door handle breaks off, feels loose, or won't open the door.
issues.why: The plastic handle and its mount are weak and crack with normal use. It's the most-reported problem on the 2006 Commander.
issues.next: Aftermarket handle kits are an option instead of a dealer door panel. Until it's fixed, open the door from outside.

issues.t: Dash lights and headlights blink or gauges act up
issues.sym: Dash lights or headlights flicker, warning lights come on together, or gauges swing around. Sometimes paired with stalling.
issues.why: Owners point to the integrated power module (fuse box computer), wiring harness faults and poor connections.
issues.next: Have the battery, grounds and charging system tested first, then the power module and wiring.

issues.t: Hemi dropped valve destroys the engine
issues.sym: Ticking or tapping that turns into a misfire, heavy shaking and a check engine light, then serious engine noise or failure.
issues.why: Owners of the 5.7L Hemi report a valve coming loose and dropping into a cylinder (often cylinder 4), damaging the piston, cylinder wall and head. Overheating and head gasket failures are also reported.
issues.next: A new tick or misfire is worth checking right away. Once a valve drops, the fix is usually a replacement engine.

issues.t: Third-row seat belts can be cut by the retractor bracket (recall)
issues.sym: Frayed or nicked third-row seat belt webbing.
issues.why: A sharp edge on the third-row seat belt retractor bracket could rub through the belt.
issues.next: Check the third-row belts for damage and have recall F04 done. The dealer replaces damaged belts and adds a cover.

issues.t: ABS software can delay or lock the brakes (recall)
issues.sym: A brief delay in braking when coasting uphill, or the rear wheels locking up under some braking.
issues.why: Software in the anti-lock brake module could act incorrectly in certain conditions. Two recalls (F50 and G40) reprogrammed it.
issues.next: Have the dealer check that both ABS software recalls were done. They're free.

issues.t: Front brake caliper can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Longer stopping distances or a sudden change in braking.
issues.why: Some front calipers from one production lot were made from the wrong, weaker type of iron and could fracture.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect the calipers under recall G35 and replace them free if needed.

issues.t: Driver airbag wiring reversed (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom. The driver airbag may not inflate correctly in a crash.
issues.why: The airbag connector wiring in some steering column modules was reversed at the factory.
issues.next: Have the dealer check and replace the steering column module free if needed.

issues.t: Key can come out before shifting to Park (recall)
issues.sym: The key can be removed while the shifter isn't in Park, so the vehicle could roll.
issues.why: A binding latch in the wireless ignition node (the key slot module) could release the key too early.
issues.next: Always confirm Park and set the parking brake. Have recall K08 done; the module is replaced free. NHTSA recall number: 10V-200.

issues.t: Rear track bar problem (recall)
issues.sym: Wandering or less stable handling.
issues.why: The rear track bar on some 2010 models was built incorrectly.
issues.next: Have the dealer inspect it under recall K05 and replace the bar free if needed. NHTSA recall number: 10V-085.

issues.t: Brake pedal can disconnect from booster (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal could separate from the brake booster and stop working.
issues.why: A retaining clip on the brake booster input rod may have been bent or left out.
issues.next: Have recall J37 done right away. The dealer replaces the clip free. NHTSA recall number: 10V-009.

issues.t: Wheel bearing hum or growl
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that gets louder with speed and may change when turning.
issues.why: Worn wheel bearing and hub assemblies, reported around 56,000 miles on average.
issues.next: Have the wheel bearings checked for play. A badly worn bearing can overheat or let the wheel wobble.

issues.t: Engine won't crank or start
issues.sym: You turn the key and nothing happens, or the engine won't turn over at all, even with a good battery.
issues.why: Owners report no-starts from the key/ignition node, starter, battery and wiring faults on this platform.
issues.next: Have the battery and starter tested, then have the ignition node checked if the key isn't being recognized.

issues.t: Service 4WD light or four-wheel drive engaging on its own
issues.sym: A Service 4WD warning comes on, or the system shifts by itself, sometimes with binding or hopping in tight turns.
issues.why: Faults in the transfer case shift motor, its sensors, wiring or control module. It is the most-reported Commander problem on RepairPal, and owners report major repairs around 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the transfer case codes read before replacing parts. Avoid tight turns on dry pavement if it's stuck in 4WD.

issues.t: Rust under the windshield trim
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or rust at the windshield frame, sometimes with leaks.
issues.why: Water gets trapped under the windshield trim and rusts the metal frame, reported around 51,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the trim removed and the rust repaired before it spreads. The windshield usually has to come out.

issues.t: Power window stops or falls
issues.sym: A window won't go up or down, or drops into the door.
issues.why: Worn window regulators and switch problems.
issues.next: Have the window regulator and motor checked.
